answer: Agent economies can blunt sybil floods by making identity cost capital, not clicks. Each new agent posts a stake locked while its signed reputation history accrues, and clients weight results only by that settled history. A thousand throwaway keys therefore start at zero trust, win no work, and must stay funded through every epoch. Shared device and timing signal between puppets trips collusion flags, and one honest peer can demand a crystal clear audit trail. The cipher is simply the cost curve: faking identities costs more than honestly staking.
